newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Ten firms bid for Tunisian power plant.
newsitem.headline: Ten firms bid for Tunisian power plant.

text.p: Ten firms are competing for a tender to build and run Tunisia's first privately-owned power plant with an estimated cost of $300 million, energy officials said on Friday.
They said the 10 firms, pre-selected last October, had been withdrawing this month the cahier des charges for the final qualification, an energy official told Reuters.
Offers are scheduled to be received by next March and the final decision is expected by the end of the year, he added.

The Independent Power Production (IPP) project is for the development of a combined-cycle gas turbine station which could supply 350-to-500 megawatts of electricity. It is to be located at Rades in southern Tunis.

The competitors are ABB Energy Ventures, British Gas, Community Energy Alternatives, Destec Energy Europe, Electricite de France EDF, Enron Development Corp., Powerfin, Intergen, National Power International, Energy Power Development Corp.
It will be the first power plant to be privately-run after Tunsia last year scratched the state monopoly on power generation and allowed private investors to run power plants.
The electricity produced is to be supplied to the state-owned Societe Tunisienne de l'Electricite et du Gaz for distribution under a long term contract.
STEG will keep its existing production plants and distribution of electricity.

Energy officials say the country needs to build one 300 megawatts plant each two to three years under the IPP formula to enable it to face increasing electricity demand which growth by an average seven per cent a year.
